      <description><p>What started as one artist’s response to being cut out of a music video has exploded, becoming a driving force in Nigeria’s cultural landscape</p><p>As a student in the central Nigerian city of Ilorin, Lawal Habeeb Kola loved staying in his hostel room to produce beats rather than returning to his family house in Lagos, the more frenetic city of his birth.</p><p>In 2022, one of his beats became popular on TikTok, and a version featuring ad-libbed vocals from a hypeman sent it viral.       <link>https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/25/people-killed-fuel-tanker-crash-ignites-large-fire-cairo-highway</link>
      <description><p>Blaze on ring road surrounding Egyptian capital injures at least 21 people and leaves cars and motorcycles charred</p><p>A crash involving a fuel tanker ignited a huge fire on a highway surrounding Cairo on Wednesday, killing at least 31 people, Egyptian authorities said.</p><p>The blaze on the ring road, a key artery that encircles the Egyptian capital, also injured at least 21 people and left more than two dozen cars and motorcycles charred, according to the latest figures released by the health ministry.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/25/people-killed-fuel-tanker-crash-ignites-large-fire-cairo-highway">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <description><p>Alain Throo, insurance executive based in London, reportedly gored and later died on hike near Mount Cameroon national park</p><p>A Swiss tourist has been killed and British and American tourists have been injured when a group of hikers encountered a herd of elephants in Cameroon.</p><p>The group of six tourists, four British, one Swiss and one American, accompanied by local guides, were hiking near the village of Bakingili in the south of the Mount Cameroon national park on 19 November, on a path used by elephants to access a nearby lake, when they encountered the herd of about 15 animals, according to media reports.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/environment/2026/nov/25/swiss-tourist-killed-british-americans-injured-elephants-cameroon">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>Three studies link glyphosate to cancer, contradicting claims of Trump EPA</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/nov/27/glyphosate-cancer-studies-trump-epa</link>
      <description><p>Experts say NIH research raises concerns about chemical companies’ influence on US agency’s pesticide division</p><p>The US government’s top medical research agency has <a href="https://zenodo.org/records/24354736">released</a> three <a href="https://zenodo.org/records/24372545">new studies</a> linking glyphosate, the world’s most widely used pesticide and an active ingredient in Roundup, <a href="https://zenodo.org/records/24356429">to cancer</a>. The National Institutes of Health (NIH) findings contradict a controversial recent Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) conclusion that the weedkiller is not a carcinogen, and deals a blow to the White House, which has been <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/environment/2026/feb/19/trump-order-protect-weedkiller">closely allied</a> with Roundup’s producer, Bayer.</p><p>The NIH’s three papers could have significant political and legal fallout. The EPA is in the process of a court-ordered re-evaluation of glyphosate’s cancer risks. The NIH findings generate new pressure for the EPA to find that the substance is linked to cancer, which would subject it to a modest increase in regulations.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/nov/27/glyphosate-cancer-studies-trump-epa">Continue reading...</a></description>
